chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, altogether from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When the soul reaches here' — and he pointed with his hand to his throat — 'there would be no repentance for the scholar.'
Then he recited: 'Indeed, repentance with God is only for those who do evil in ignorance.'

key_terms.التوبة: Repentance (tawbah) — returning to God after sin; the accepted repentance
key_terms.العالم: The scholar/learned person — one who possesses religious knowledge
key_terms.النفس: The soul/life force — here referring to the soul departing at the point of death
key_terms.بجهالة: In ignorance — the condition under which repentance is accepted per Quran 4:17

ai.seo_question: Why does Imam al-Sadiq say there is no repentance for a scholar at the time of death?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) warns that a scholar who neglects to act upon his knowledge loses the opportunity for repentance at the moment of death. The Imam dramatizes this by pointing to his throat — indicating the moment when the soul departs — and then recites Quran 4:17, which limits accepted repentance to those who act out of ignorance. The implication is that a scholar, unlike an ignorant person, cannot claim ignorance as an excuse, making their accountability far greater.
